(a) Strategic Policy Required.—Chapter 131 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section:“§ 2229. Strategic policy on prepositioning of materiel and equipment“(a) Policy Required.—The Secretary of Defense shall maintain a strategic policy on the programs of the Department of Defense for the prepositioning of materiel and equipment. Such policy shall take into account national security threats, strategic mobility, service requirements, and the requirements of the combatant commands.“(b) Limitation of Diversion of Prepositioned Materiel.—The Secretary of a military department may not divert materiel or equipment from prepositioned stocks except—“(1) in accordance with a change made by the Secretary of Defense to the policy maintained under subsection (a); or“(2) for the purpose of directly supporting a contingency operation or providing humanitarian assistance under chapter 20 of this title.“(c) Congressional Notification.—The Secretary of Defense may not implement or change the policy required under subsection (a) until the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees a report describing the policy or change to the policy.”
. 
    (b) Clerical Amendment.—The table of sections at the beginning of such chapter is amended by adding at the end the following new item:


“2229. 
Strategic policy on prepositioning of materiel and equipment.”.

 
    (c) Deadline for Establishment of Policy.—
        (1) Deadline.—Not later than six months after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall establish the strategic policy on the programs of the Department of Defense for the prepositioning of materiel and equipment required under section 2229 of title 10, United States Code, as added by subsection (a). 
        (2) Limitation on diversion of prepositioned materiel.—During the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on the date on which the Secretary of Defense submits the report required under section 2229(c) of title 10, United States Code, on the policy referred to in paragraph (1), the Secretary of a military department may not divert materiel or equipment from prepositioned stocks except for the purpose of directly supporting a contingency operation or providing humanitarian assistance under chapter 20 of that title.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the precondition of reporting to the congressional defense committees before implementing or changing the policy is a form of consultation. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so this is intra-governmental notification rather than participation. The policy is an internal Department of Defense strategic policy, with no rulemaking, public comment, advisory body, or consultation with states, experts, or other outside parties.
fable.s: The Secretary of Defense may not implement or change the policy required under subsection (a) until the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees a report describing the policy or change to the policy.

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to congressional defense committees before implementing a policy. Congress and its committees are considered inside the federal government. Therefore, this is an intra-governmental notification requirement, not participation by outside parties.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of Defense may not implement or change the policy required under subsection (a) until the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees a report describing the policy or change to the policy.

opus.w: The only step required before the decision is a report to the congressional defense committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The other parties the policy must account for are the military services and the combatant commands, which are also federal. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to sue.
opus.s: The Secretary of Defense may not implement or change the policy required under subsection (a) until the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees a report describing the policy or change to the policy.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the Secretary cannot implement or change the policy until submitting a report to the congressional defense committees. That looks like a required step before a decision. But Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so this is a report to Congress, not outside participation.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to congressional defense committees before implementing a policy. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this notification is intra-governmental coordination and does not involve consultation or coordination with people outside the government.
qwen_chat.s: (c) Congressional Notification.—The Secretary of Defense may not implement or change the policy required under subsection (a) until the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees a report describing the policy or change to the policy.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement to submit a report to congressional defense committees constitutes "participation" because it involves an external check on the Secretary's decision. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
